correctness.rationale: For any wheel spanning tree T, graphic-matroid exchange distances and the maximum forest rank of the complementary subgraph prove ecc(T)=m-beta(H_T). Every complementary wheel cycle uses at least three edges, and rim degrees <=2 force distinct cycles to share at most the hub, giving beta<=floor(m/3). Explicit q disjoint hub triangles plus r spokes attain the bound, while an explicit complementary tree attains diameter m. For the periphery, each nonconstant binary rim coloring has exactly two spoke completions, by alternation at the even number of run boundaries, and both colors then form trees. Two standalone Python verifiers pass complete finite exhaustive checks, including all tree pairs for m<=5.

value.rationale: The full center/periphery metric classification is a natural missing numerical refinement of the existing general tree-graph complement theory. The explicit count of all peripheral labelled spanning trees is a genuine closed enumerative result, not a substitution into a known total tree-count formula. It answers intrinsic network exchange questions for an infinite family and supplies checkable algorithmic benchmarks.
